item.title: Page updated: Kennebec County Registry of Deeds — Kennebec County Registry of Deeds
item.description:
This page's content changed since the last check. Visit the page directly to review the update.
What changed (text excerpt): Added: + Registry of Deeds + The Kennebec County Registry of Deeds has proudly served our community since 1799, safeguarding the essential property records that form the foundation of real estate ownership. + As required by Maine law, the Registry meticulously maintains and preserves all recorded documents and plans from historical deeds dating back over 200 years to today’s modern transactions. + Our office provides prompt, professional, and courteous service to the public, making vital records such as mortgages, deeds, liens, and plans easily accessible. Every document is carefully preserved for the permanent record. + Records are available for convenient public search both online and in our office, supporting homeowners, real estate professionals, title companies, and businesses throughout Kennebec County. + The Registry is led by Register of Deeds Matthew Boucher, with dedicated support from Deputy Register Sue Lapointe and a committed team. + Whether you’re researching property history, closing a real estate transaction, or ensuring clear title, the Kennebec County Registry of Deeds stands ready to serve you with accuracy, efficiency, and a strong commitment to customer service. + Property Alert + SIGN UP NOW + Search + Public Records Removed: - Click here to search - public records - Click here to sign up for property alert - Matthew Boucher - Register of Deeds

item.title: Page updated: York County Registry of Deeds — York County Registry of Deeds
item.description:
This page's content changed since the last check. Visit the page directly to review the update.
What changed (text excerpt): Added: + Spring/summer online debut planned for historical York County records + ALFRED, Maine – In May 1835, Ivory R. Hatch, who lived in the town of Wells, was unhappy with the result of an interaction with the town concerning a portion of his land. Wells selectmen had undertaken to lay out a road – an important decision at a time when there weren’t many roads. The new road, to be 3 rods, or 49.5 feet wide, was to be built on several portions of privately held land – including 72 rods, or 1,188 feet – of Hatch’s property. “Aggrieved,” in the amount of + Tammy L Wells + 1 day ago + 4 min read Removed: - Seeing history, up close - While people drive by the 1806 York County Court House in Alfred every day, many may have never been inside, and fewer still may know how much history lives in this county-owned building. - Tammy L Wells - Oct 2, 2025 - 6 min read
